# WCAG Check

> A free tool that checks whether a web page meets the accessibility requirements of the European Accessibility Act. It reports each problem against both its WCAG 2.2 success criterion and the corresponding EN 301 549 clause 9 reference, which is the standard the Act actually cites.

Enter a page URL and two engines run against it: about 95 axe-core rules in your own
browser, and 20 static HTML rules on the server. Results are generated per request;
nothing about a scanned site is stored, and no account is needed.

## What it detects

- Colour contrast, for the part of the page that fits on screen
- Element-level problems across roughly 95 axe-core rules covering WCAG 2.2 Level A
  and AA: accessible names, ARIA validity, form labelling, landmark structure,
  heading order, list semantics, table headers, frame titles and more
- Page-level problems the element scan cannot see: missing title, missing lang
  attribute, no h1, no main landmark

Findings that map to a WCAG success criterion are reported as EN 301 549
requirements. Rules that are only best practice are reported separately, so a
compliance count is never inflated by things the law does not require. Results the
engine could not decide are shown as needing review and are never counted as passes.

## What it cannot detect

- Content built by JavaScript. Scripts on the scanned page are never executed. This
  is a deliberate security decision rather than a gap to be fixed
- Colour contrast below the area that fits on screen. Contrast can only be judged
  for content genuinely rendered in the viewport
- The roughly two thirds of WCAG criteria that require human judgement

A clean result means the machine-detectable problems are gone, not that a site is
compliant.

## Limits worth knowing

Some sites reject automated requests at their gateway (HTTP 403, 429 or 511). Those
cannot be checked from here and the tool says so plainly rather than reporting the
site as broken. Roughly 40% of large retail sites fall into this category; small
business sites far less often.

## Pages

- [Home and scanner](https://wcagcheck.eu/): run a check and read the report

## References

- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/): the W3C accessibility guidelines
- [EN 301 549](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/): the European standard whose clause 9 restates WCAG Level A and AA for websites
- [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core): the analysis engine, MPL-2.0, used unmodified
